newsitem.title: USA: Komag shares gain on comments about yields.
newsitem.headline: Komag shares gain on comments about yields.

text.p: Komag Inc shares gained after company officials made comments at an investor conference reiterating the progress it has made boosting the quality, or yield, of its disk drive components, a Komag spokesman said.

Ted Siegler, director of corporate planning at Komag, tied the stock surge to the conference presentation, but said Komag officials were merely reiterating previous statements about their efforts to improve manufacturing yields.
Komag shares closed Wednesday up 3-5/8 points at 31-5/8.

The company's problems with yields, or the percentage of semicondutor chips considered usable versus the chips that must be thrown out in any production run, had caused its fourth quarter results to suffer, analysts said.

Wednesday afternoon, Komag told an audience attending a Goldman Sachs technology conference here that yields are "getting better" and its outlook for 1997 is generally more positive, according to Rick Shutte, a Goldman analyst.
"Everyone's focus is so much on yields in this segment," the analyst said of the importance investors place on this measure of the company's performance.
Shutte said he maintains a $0.30 per share estimate on Komag's first quarter, putting him on the high side of the Wall Street consensus estimate, which stands at $0.25 per share.
"I am pretty happy with that estimate," Shutte said.
